title: [cutover prerequisite] Durable cutover generation evidence and its production reader: distribution manifest, import generation, quiesce record digests
description:
FILED BY architect-1270c677 on 2026-08-29 at HEAD aebdb367, as the measured prerequisite that hard-blocks task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9 (Cutover activation tooling). The epic rails require prerequisite production tasks with the gap measured symbol by symbol rather than a narrowed DoD or a mock-backed journey; this is that row.

WHAT BLOCKS. task-b2548479's daemon `cutover.activate` must write a v2 activation marker recording the CURRENT generation snapshot at activation time. The marker module already exists as that row's WIP (apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activation-marker.ts, untracked) and it CONSUMES the tuple — `:30` declares `readonly distributionManifestSha256: string` and `:109` reads `input.generations.distributionManifestSha256`. It does not produce it. Nothing else does either, so the values could only come from the caller, and caller-supplied current values would FABRICATE BOTH SIDES of the drift comparison the marker exists to make. That is the exact class of fabricated-authority defect these epics exist to remove.

THE GAP, MEASURED SYMBOL BY SYMBOL at HEAD aebdb367, tracked, repo-wide:
- `distributionManifestSha256` — appears ONLY in packages/benchmark/src/activation-binding.ts, activation-binding.test.ts, activation-record.test.ts. All CONSUMER sites; the admission takes it as input. `git grep -ln 'distributionManifest\|distribution-manifest' HEAD -- apps packages tools` returns only control-room live-dispatch.ts (a DEV_PAYLOADS fixture) and daemon http/bootstrap TEST fixtures. NO durable producer.
- `importGenerationSha256` — appears ONLY in those same three packages/benchmark files. NO producer.
- `quiesceRecordSha256` — same three files only. The live legacy quiesce apparatus landed (tests/migration/cutover-live/live-quiesce-*.ts, commit e73e3aa7) but emits NO digest: `git grep -n 'sha256\|digest\|Digest' HEAD -- tests/migration/cutover-live/live-quiesce-evidence.ts` returns EMPTY.
- `backupGenerationDigest` — this ONE is different and must be composed, not rebuilt. It has a rich durable surface already under apps/daemon/src/recovery/ (recovery-inventory-reader.ts, recovery-inventory-record.ts, recovery-incarnation.ts, recovery-succession.ts, recovery-completion-evidence.ts, durable-recovery-inventory-reader.ts and others).

Also measured absent in the daemon: no `CutoverAttemptState` and no `reduceCutover` consumer or writer (`grep -rn 'reduceCutover\|CutoverAttemptState' apps/daemon/src` is EMPTY, untracked-inclusive), and no authoritative-v2 command gate reads ACTIVE or the marker. `reduceCutover` itself IS landed and barrel-reachable (packages/core/src/cutover/cutover-reducer.ts:235, exported at packages/core/src/index.ts:403).

SCOPE. Land durable, digestible evidence for the three producerless generations, and ONE production reader that returns the four-value snapshot from durable state for a given cutover attempt. NOT IN SCOPE: task-b2548479's marker or daemon service (it consumes this), task-b8272ee0's roster registration, task-c4321b6f's GA execution, and the recovery journey's existing backup evidence, which must be COMPOSED rather than duplicated.

THIS ROW MAY ITSELF NEED SPLITTING. Three independent evidence producers plus a reader may exceed the ten-file plan cap; if the planning architect measures that, split by producer and land the reader last. Say which shape was chosen and why.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, learned expensively on this board today: an ABSENCE premise must be probed UNTRACKED-INCLUSIVE. `git grep <rev>` reads the commit and is blind to untracked files by construction — a producer row was filed this morning for work a live worker had already written in the worktree. Probe with `git status --porcelain` or a worktree `grep -r` ALONGSIDE the HEAD grep, and scan non-terminal rows for the deliverable's filenames before building.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, recorded in a durable moe.add_comment (the completion summary is write-only and persists nowhere). Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it beside every probe, each UNPIPED with its own exit code and a positive control. Re-run the gap measurement BOTH tracked and untracked-inclusive: for each of distributionManifestSha256, importGenerationSha256 and quiesceRecordSha256 confirm there is still no durable producer, using `git grep -n <sym> HEAD -- apps packages tools` AND a worktree `grep -rn <sym> apps packages tools`. If a producer now exists, ADOPT it and report blocked as duplicate rather than building a second one. Also scan non-terminal rows for these symbols before writing any byte.

Each of the three producerless generations has a DURABLE, SERVER-DERIVED digest recorded by production code - the digest is computed from the artifact it names, never supplied or influenced by a caller, and a caller-presented digest is REFUSED with an exact stable reason code at a named layer, both asserted. For the quiesce record specifically, compose the landed live-quiesce apparatus (tests/migration/cutover-live/) as the artifact source rather than inventing a parallel notion of what quiescence means.

backupGenerationDigest is COMPOSED, NOT REBUILT. It is read through the existing durable recovery surface under apps/daemon/src/recovery/ - name in a row comment exactly which reader you compose and why it is the right one. A fourth notion of backup generation that agrees with the recovery lane today will drift from it tomorrow; that is the same third-notion hazard the board has already been burned by on policy refs.

ONE PRODUCTION READER returns the complete four-value snapshot for a given cutover attempt from durable state, and REFUSES deterministically when any of the four is unavailable - naming WHICH fact was missing, with its exact code and refusing layer. Absence must refuse, never default to a zero digest or an empty string: a zero-filled generation would silently compare equal to another zero-filled one and make the drift comparison vacuous.

RAIL 8(B) CONSUMER EDGE: name task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9 as the consumer and record its id in a row comment. A reader nothing imports satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist. If one durable call site can be landed without reaching into that row's scope, prefer it and say what you did.

Round-trip and tamper proof over a FILE-BACKED store: each recorded generation reads back byte-identical through the reader; a mutated byte refuses with the exact code; an identical re-record adds ZERO duplicate decision and event rows, asserted as counts with denominators. Mutation drills each redden a NAMED arm - substituting a zero digest for the refusal must red the absence arm, and substituting a DIFFERENT default must red the SAME arm, since absence and a defaulted value are different answers.

Gates standalone, foreground and unpiped, each with exit code AND nonzero count line quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 quoting its `$ tsc` echo, and the focused daemon suite quoting its `Test Files`/`Tests` counts - the root vitest include has NO apps/**, so a bare `pnpm test` runs zero daemon tests and proves nothing here. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus delivered owned-path delta with foreign failures disclosed verbatim. Every production file under 400 lines; every new `.ts` with its `.js` bridge; explicit-pathspec commit, never `git add -A`.
taskRails: Never accept a caller-supplied generation digest and never default an absent one to zeros or an empty string. The marker exists to detect drift; a caller-supplied or defaulted value fabricates both sides of that comparison and makes the whole mechanism decorative.

Compose the existing surfaces rather than duplicating them: the recovery lane for backupGenerationDigest, and the landed live-quiesce apparatus for the quiesce artifact. Do not introduce a second notion of either. State in a row comment which reader/artifact you composed and why.

An ABSENCE premise must be probed UNTRACKED-INCLUSIVE - `git grep <rev>` reads the commit and cannot see untracked files. Pair every HEAD grep with `git status --porcelain` or a worktree `grep -r`, and scan non-terminal rows for the deliverable's filenames. A duplicate producer row was filed on this board today for exactly this reason.
This row lands the evidence and its reader. It does NOT implement task-b2548479's marker or daemon cutover.activate service, task-b8272ee0's roster registration, or task-c4321b6f's GA execution.

Shared worktree: commit only owned pathspecs, never `git add -A`; preserve foreign WIP including the untracked apps/daemon/src/cutover/ directory, which is task-b2548479's; no push, no PR comment. Mutation drills in a temp copy or with a restore proven in a call SEPARATE from the restore, by SHA256 for untracked paths since `git diff` is blind to them.
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure every cited line number and symbol at claim time - they move. If a sibling landed the mechanism first, verify and close rather than re-implement.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 2 — RED FIRST, and it can be authored before the children land.

Create `apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-generation-snapshot.test.ts` with the arms the reader must satisfy. They will RED until step 3 exists, and the two child-dependent arms will RED until the children land — that is expected and is the honest TDD signal, not a blocker for this step.

ARMS:
(1) ACCEPTED CONTROL — a store holding all four durable facts yields a complete four-value snapshot, each value EQUAL to what the durable source independently returns. Assert equality against the durable read, never against a literal: a literal is a fixed point and a hardcoded-return mutant passes it.
(2) FOUR ABSENCE ARMS, one per generation — with that one fact unavailable the reader REFUSES, naming WHICH fact was missing, with its exact stable code AND refusing layer. Four separate arms, not one parameterised arm asserting "it refused": a single arm cannot tell you the reader names the right fact.
(3) NEVER-DEFAULT ARM — no path returns a zero digest or an empty string for any generation. A zero-filled generation compares equal to another zero-filled one and makes the drift comparison this snapshot exists for silently vacuous.
(4) CALLER-PRESENTED ARM — a caller cannot supply or influence any of the four; the reader takes an attempt identity, not digests. Make that structurally impossible in the signature where you can, and refused with a named code where you cannot.

SHARED-DIRECTORY CAUTION: `apps/daemon/src/cutover/` already holds task-b2548479's UNTRACKED WIP (cutover-activation-marker.{ts,js,test.ts}). Add your files beside them; never edit or stage theirs. `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/cutover/` before and after, and commit by explicit pathspec naming only your own files.

STEP 3 — THE COMPOSING READER. New module `apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-generation-snapshot.ts` (<=250 lines target, 400 hard) plus its one-line bridge `cutover-generation-snapshot.js` containing exactly `export * from "./cutover-generation-snapshot.ts";` — the js-bridge rule: tsc and vitest resolve without it, plain Node does not.

GATED ON BOTH CHILDREN per step 1. Do not begin until their production surfaces are on disk.

THE SEAM: given a cutover attempt identity (and the project), return the complete four-value generation snapshot read from DURABLE state. It COMPOSES four sources and derives nothing itself:
  distributionManifestSha256 <- the durable project record's `distributionManifestHash`
  backupGenerationDigest     <- the source you named in step 1(b)
  quiesceRecordSha256        <- task-2bf8fa1a's production serializer
  importGenerationSha256     <- task-f25077c5's durable source
Every value server-derived; the reader accepts NO digest from any caller.

REFUSE, NEVER DEFAULT. When any one of the four is unavailable the reader returns a refusal NAMING that fact, with an exact stable code and its layer. Do not return a partial snapshot and do not zero-fill: a partial snapshot is the invented-absence failure the recovery reader's own doc comment warns about at durable-recovery-inventory-reader.ts:312-314 ("an inventory that answers with whatever it happened to find is the invented absence this area prevents") — the same standard applies here.

RAIL 8(B) CONSUMER EDGE: name `task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9` as this reader's consumer and record its id in a row comment. That row's marker module already CONSUMES a generations tuple (cutover-activation-marker.ts:109 reads `input.generations.*`), which is exactly the shape this reader returns — but wiring it is THAT row's step, not this one's. Do not edit their marker.

STEP 4 — ROUND-TRIP AND TAMPER OVER A FILE-BACKED STORE. Discharges the parent DoD's round-trip clause.

Drive a REAL file-backed store, never an in-memory stub: each generation recorded by its producer reads back byte-identical through this snapshot reader; a mutated byte in any one of the four refuses with that generation's exact code; and re-reading the same attempt is stable — identical inputs yield an identical snapshot with ZERO additional decision and event rows, asserted as COUNTS WITH DENOMINATORS, not as "no error".

Also assert the snapshot is ATTEMPT-SCOPED: two different cutover attempts against the same project do not silently share a snapshot. If the design makes them share by construction, say so and prove it is correct rather than asserting a property that cannot fail.

STEP 5 — MUTATION DRILLS, each redding a NAMED arm. All four owned files are NEW and therefore UNTRACKED (`??`) until committed — `git diff` is BLIND to them, so prove EVERY restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree %TEMP% backup suffixed with your worker id, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Two empty hashes compare equal and print match:true, so assert both are 64 hex chars AND equal.

D1 DEFAULT INSTEAD OF REFUSE: substitute a zero digest for one generation's absence refusal — that generation's NAMED absence arm must RED.
D2 A DIFFERENT DEFAULT: substitute a different non-zero literal for the same absence — the SAME arm must RED. Both drills are required: absence and a defaulted value are different answers, and one drill alone cannot show the arm distinguishes them.
D3 WRONG SOURCE: point one generation at a different durable field of the same shape — the accepted control must RED on that value's equality assertion. This is what proves the reader composes the RIGHT four sources rather than four plausible ones.
D4 PARTIAL SNAPSHOT: make the reader return three values and omit the fourth instead of refusing — a named arm must RED. A partial snapshot passing would mean the invented-absence failure is reachable.
A GREEN DRILL IS A FINDING to report in a comment and stop on, never a pass to bank.

STEP 6 — GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE RECORD, PATHSPEC COMMIT.

GATES — FOREGROUND, UNPIPED, ONE PER CALL, each with exit code AND count line. A piped run reports the tail's exit code; an exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING and is UNVERIFIED.
LEG A: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — exit 0, quote the `$ tsc` echo as execution evidence. This leg runs even on the blocked path from step 1, since it proves the row left the tree compiling.
LEG B: the focused suite over cutover-generation-snapshot.test.ts — exit 0, `Test Files` and `Tests` counts quoted, both nonzero.
LEG C: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` by PATH ATTRIBUTION — failures at the merge-base vs at HEAD, delta intersected with this row's owned paths must be EMPTY; foreign red disclosed VERBATIM.
NOTE the root vitest include has NO apps/**, so a bare `pnpm test` runs ZERO daemon tests and proves nothing here.
SIZE: every production file <= 400 lines (250 target); every new `.ts` carries its `.js` bridge.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, each answered with a measurement or an explicit N/A: what happens when the project record is re-activated between reading one generation and the next (is the snapshot torn, and what orders them); whether two concurrent cutover attempts can interleave reads; whether any of the four values can reach a log, argv or refusal detail; whether a caller can influence ANY of the four through the attempt identity alone; and whether the reader holds a store handle open on every exit path including a thrown one.

RECORD via moe.add_comment — the completion summary is write-only and persists nowhere. Carry: step 1's corrected four-way measurement with HEAD quoted, INCLUDING which backupGenerationDigest source you chose and why; the child-gate outcome; all four drill results with the arm each redded; every gate's exit and counts; the foreign-red disclosure. Name task-b254847909ca4199a70a3a06173f1cd9 as the consumer. Keep each comment under ~4500 chars and SPLIT rather than truncate.
COMMIT by explicit pathspec naming ONLY your own three files. `apps/daemon/src/cutover/` also holds task-b2548479's untracked marker WIP — never `git add -A`, never stage that directory wholesale, and confirm with `git show --stat <sha>` that the commit names your files and nothing else. No push, no PR comment.

STEP 1 BLOCKER — the approved plan's required source premises do not exist in production, so a six-file injected-port implementation would be port/mock-shaped authority rather than a working cutover snapshot.

1) DISTRIBUTION. There is no singular durable distribution-manifest artifact. buildDistributionContainer returns ephemeral per-component canonical `manifestBytes` (distribution-build.ts:61,197-208). DISTRIBUTION_INVENTORY is six components; release-subject keeps bytes only in memory and supply-chain retains each component's digest. At HEAD a3849db9: `git grep -n 'writeFile.*manifestBytes\|persist.*manifestBytes' HEAD -- tools/packaging scripts/release` => no output, exit 1; positive control `git grep -n manifestBytes ...` => build/release hits, exit 0. The singular field is also ambiguous over six manifests. apps/daemon cannot import tools/* (not a workspace package; rootDir=src).

2) BACKUP. readDurableRecoveryInventory is a validator, not a producer: it requires rawBasis containing backupGenerationDigest, then lines 179-180 compare the RESTORE anchor generation to that supplied basis. Its success shape omits the digest. Therefore using it to source the value is circular and violates the no-caller-generation rail. A viable source is ACTIVE recovery binding -> readAnchoredIncarnation RESTORE binding, but the full project/ref/key-epoch validation needs a public recovery reader or an explicit plan amendment.

3) QUIESCE. serializeLiveEvidence exists only at tests/migration/cutover-live/live-quiesce-evidence.ts:209; tests/** is outside daemon rootDir, has no .js bridge/package export, and cannot be statically imported into production. Safe choices require amendment: hash the exact durable file bytes written by that apparatus via a real production file reader, or promote the serializer/shape to a production/shared module and repoint the harness. Do not copy JSON.stringify.

4) IMPORT. tools/import persists the import effect but exposes no standalone generation artifact/reader; commitLegacyImport drops the store receipt's effectSha256 and import-commit prints non-durable stdout JSON. The strongest existing server-derived identity is SqliteEventStore.getCommandReceipt(commandId).effectSha256, re-proven from durable rows, but choosing it (plus schema-integrity semantics) is a product/plan decision, not the planned artifact-byte port.

Requested unblock: split/land a packaging producer for one canonical ordered distribution-generation artifact + daemon-reachable reader; expose a recovery current-backup-generation reader; choose the quiesce durable-file composition; define/import the validated import-generation authority. Then amend this row's owned paths and tests. Implementing now would fabricate the current-side evidence the marker is meant to trust.
